title: Rowlandton Mound Site (15McN3): Mississippian Town in McCracken County
summary: In McCracken County, the Rowlandton Mound Site (15MCN3) was a Mississippian town with a large platform mound, lived in from about 1100 to 1350 CE.
bodyMarkdown:
The Rowlandton Mound Site (15MCN3) is a Mississippian town site in McCracken County. People lived there from about 1100 to about 1350 CE. The 3-hectare (7.4-acre) site has a large platform mound and an associated village area, roughly the size of the Wickliffe Mounds site in far western Kentucky.

Archaeologists once thought that large civic centers in western Kentucky such as Rowlandton, Twin Mounds and Tolu were 13th-century expansions of the Kincaid Mounds polity in southern Illinois, but excavations in 2006 by Kit Wesler of Murray State University showed that this was not the case; the centers were probably founded by local Late Woodland peoples. The map pin is generalized to protect the site.
Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowlandton_Mound_Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowlandton_Mound_Site)
